episode.title: Recognize an official model alias when assigning context and output budgets
episode.before: At parent commit 156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe, the ordered input-limit table recognized only names beginning with `deepseek-v4` as the 1,000,000-token tier. The official `deepseek-flash` name therefore matched the later generic `deepseek` rule and received 131,072 input tokens. The output-limit table likewise recognized only `deepseek-v4`; `deepseek-flash` matched no output-specific rule and fell back through `tokenLimit` to the 32,000-token default. Consequently, configuration initialized from that official name could use budgets inconsistent with the model's V4 limits, which the resolution commit associates with long-session compaction output truncation.
episode.after: At commit 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864, both ordered limit tables use the specific pattern `^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)` before the generic family rule. Thus `deepseek-flash` resolves to a 1,000,000-token input window and a 384,000-token output limit, while existing older-family names such as `deepseek-r1`, `deepseek-v3`, and `deepseek-chat` retain their established fallback behavior. A focused regression test asserts both corrected values.
episode.diff: The implementation broadened two coordinated regular expressions in `packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts`: the input classifier changed from `^deepseek-v4` to `^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)` for the 1M tier, and the output classifier made the equivalent change for the 384K tier. An explanatory comment documents why the official alias must precede the generic 128K family rule. `packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts` added one regression case asserting `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash') === 1000000` and `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash', 'output') === 384000`; neighboring tests continue to assert the generic family mappings.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864 has parent 156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe, closes issue 11894, and states that the official `deepseek-flash` name fell through to generic 128K/32K limits, causing long sessions to fail with `COMPRESSION_FAILED_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`.
evidence_units.source: `git show --format=fuller 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864`; issue-bundle.json linked PR 11909 and commit metadata

evidence_units.claim: In the parent implementation, the ordered input table placed `[/^deepseek-v4/, LIMITS['1m']]` before `[/^deepseek/, LIMITS['128k']]`; therefore `deepseek-flash` selected the generic 128K rule rather than the V4-specific rule.

In the parent implementation, the output table had a 384K rule only for `^deepseek-v4` and no generic `^deepseek` output rule. The exported `tokenLimit` function returns `DEFAULT_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT` (32,000) when no output pattern is known.
evidence_units.source: `git show 156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe:packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts`, OUTPUT_PATTERNS DeepSeek section and `tokenLimit` fallback

evidence_units.claim: The change replaces both V4-only classifiers with `^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)`, assigning the official flash alias to the 1M input and 384K output tiers while leaving the later generic input rule in place.

The post-change comment records that the official API uses `deepseek-flash`, that the alternate V4.1 spelling belongs to another endpoint, and that the alias must not fall through to the 128K family rule.
The added regression case asserts that `deepseek-flash` resolves to 1,000,000 input tokens and 384,000 output tokens.
evidence_units.source: `git show 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864:packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts`, DeepSeek test block lines corresponding to added assertions

evidence_units.claim: Neighboring tests assert that existing V4 names remain at 1M and that `deepseek-r1`, `deepseek-v3`, and `deepseek-chat` remain at the 128K input-family limit, providing a regression boundary around the broadened match.

The `tokenLimit` API is documented in implementation code as being used primarily during configuration initialization to auto-detect context-window and output-generation limits; initialized runtime code then consumes `contextWindowSize` and `maxOutputTokens`.
The pinned commit changes exactly two files, with 12 insertions and 2 deletions: the token-limit implementation and its unit test.

The focused test is a direct deterministic oracle for both affected classification dimensions: input context budget and maximum output budget. Test execution status is unavailable because the supplied working tree has its tracked files staged as deleted, so validation is grounded in the committed test rather than a new local run.
evidence_units.source: Committed assertions in `packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts`; read-only `git status --short --branch` inspection of the supplied checkout

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a supported model alias from receiving undersized context and output budgets that can trigger premature or truncated long-session compaction.

semantic_action.pre_state: A supported official model identifier misses the specific capability rules, selects a generic input-family fallback, and uses the default output fallback.

semantic_action.validation: Resolve the affected identifier for both input and output limit types and compare the returned values with the model's intended capability tiers; also check representative broader-family identifiers for unchanged fallback behavior.

candidate_workflows.name: repair-model-alias-budget-resolution
candidate_workflows.title: Repair context and output budgeting for a supported model alias
candidate_workflows.description: A bounded workflow for correcting an official model name that falls through ordered capability tables and destabilizes long-session compaction, while preserving existing family fallbacks.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a supported official model identifier initializes configuration with its actual input-context and output-generation budgets instead of generic defaults, without changing unrelated model-family behavior.
when_to_use: A supported model alias is accepted by the endpoint but resolves to a generic or default token limit.
Long sessions or compaction fail because the configured context or output budget is lower than the model capability associated with an equivalent versioned name.
Input and output capabilities are maintained in separate ordered classifiers that can drift or fall through independently.
anti_goals: Do not globally raise default context or output limits to accommodate one alias.
Do not reorder or broaden generic family rules in a way that upgrades older models without evidence.
Do not change the compaction algorithm when the demonstrated defect is capability classification.
Do not accept endpoint-incompatible spellings as a substitute for recognizing the endpoint's official identifier.
not_applicable_when: The model identifier is not supported by the target endpoint.
The authoritative model capability is unknown or disputed.
The failure persists when configuration already contains the correct input and output budgets.
The repository does not derive runtime context or output budgets from model-name classification.
inputs: The ordered input and output classifier tables
Representative specific-family and generic-family regression examples
workflow_graph.entry_state: The endpoint-accepted alias misses at least one specific capability classifier and receives a generic or default budget inconsistent with its intended model tier.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The alias resolves to the intended input and output budgets through specific rules ordered before broader fallbacks, and committed regression assertions cover both dimensions plus unaffected family behavior.

steps.condition: Apply when direct inspection proves that the official identifier falls through one or both ordered capability tables.
steps.validation: Static inspection shows the alias is covered by the specific rule before the generic family rule in both input and output classifiers.

steps.condition: Run after both classifier mappings express the intended capability contract.
steps.validation: The focused oracle asserts the exact input and output values, while adjacent family assertions constrain unintended widening.

validation_ladder: Inspect the pre-change ordered classifiers and calculate which specific, generic, or default branches the alias selects.
Inspect the post-change classifiers to confirm both input and output dimensions recognize the alias before broader fallbacks.
Run or evaluate the focused unit assertions for the alias's exact input and output limits.
Run neighboring family assertions to detect unintended classifier widening.
If the checkout is executable, run the package's focused token-limit test target; otherwise record execution as deferred rather than claiming a pass.
stop_conditions: Stop if no authoritative input and output limits can be established for the alias.
Stop if the identifier is rejected by the endpoint; classification changes cannot repair endpoint incompatibility.
Stop and investigate another layer if the alias already resolves to the correct limits.
Do not claim runtime validation when the committed test cannot be executed in the supplied checkout.
